facts.text: Operator reaction time is the interval between a warning or the appearance of a hazard and the moment the operator begins to act, such as pressing the brake.
facts.quote: Operator reaction time is the time between a warning (or the appearance of a hazard) and the moment the operator begins to act, for example by pressing the brake.

facts.text: During operator reaction time, the machine keeps moving at full speed; reaction distance equals speed multiplied by reaction time (d_reaction = v * t).
facts.quote:
During the reaction time the machine keeps moving at full speed, so the distance it covers is speed multiplied by time:

`d_reaction = v * t`

facts.text: At 40 km/h (about 11.1 m/s), a 2 s reaction time gives 22.2 m of travel before braking begins.
facts.quote: At 40 km/h (about 11.1 m/s) a reaction time of 2 s means 22.2 m before braking even begins.

facts.text: Queensland guidance uses the 40 km/h, 2 s delay example as an illustrative combined operator-plus-mechanical delay, not as a measured human reaction time.
facts.quote: Queensland guidance uses this example as a combined operator-plus-mechanical delay for illustration, not as a measured human value [Chapter 4].

facts.text: The booklet found no representative, field-measured distribution of heavy-machine operators' reaction times to proximity warnings.
facts.quote: no representative, field-measured distribution of heavy-machine operators' reaction times to proximity warnings was found [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Reaction-time values used for heavy-machine warnings include borrowed values of 0.5 to 1 s from road research, rather than validated heavy-machine field measurements.
facts.quote: The values in use are borrowed or illustrative: 0.5 to 1 s from road research

facts.text: A US regulatory brake-test table uses about 1 s as a reaction-time value; the booklet identifies values in use as borrowed or illustrative.
facts.quote: about 1 s in a US regulatory brake-test table

facts.text: A mining-truck patent uses a reaction-time margin of 1 to 3 s; the booklet identifies values in use as borrowed or illustrative.
facts.quote: 1 to 3 s as a margin in a mining-truck patent

facts.text: Road-design manuals use a reaction-time value of 2.5 s; the booklet identifies values in use as borrowed or illustrative.
Road research finds that brake responses depend on how fast the gap is closing.
facts.quote: Road research adds that brake responses depend on how fast the gap is closing

facts.text: In road research, the estimated benefit of a warning system ranged from 53% to 96% depending on the driver model chosen.
facts.quote: the estimated benefit of a warning system ranged from 53% to 96% depending on which driver model was chosen [Chapter 4].

facts.text: A Collision Mitigation System acts when the operator has not acted, so the system's waiting time depends on an assumption about operator reaction time.
facts.quote: A Collision Mitigation System acts when the operator has not, so the time the system waits is a bet on the operator's reaction time.

facts.text: The booklet recommends treating operator reaction time as an uncertain parameter and running sensitivity analyses, rather than presenting one average as validated.
facts.quote: The booklet advises treating that time as an uncertain parameter and running sensitivity analyses, not presenting one average as validated [Chapter 4].
